findings.title: [Q1.1] Business Discovery happy path has zero test or recorded-run evidence
findings.issue: The only lookup test is the Meta-unconfigured 503 case. No test, fixture, or captured run proves a non-null business_discovery response is parsed into BusinessDiscoveryResponse and persisted at ExternalCreatorService.java:262-264. A field-name or shape mismatch in the DTO would ship undetected.
findings.fix: Add a WireMock/recorded-fixture test that feeds a captured Graph business_discovery body through InstagramInsightsClient.businessDiscovery and asserts the resulting external_creators row (ig_account_id, followers, media_count) before App Review.
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/test/java/com/influora/service/BusinessDiscoveryResponseJsonMappingTest.java:60 deserializes a captured Graph business_discovery body through a real ObjectMapper and asserts every persisted field; projection matches the DTO at influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/integration/meta/client/InstagramInsightsClient.java:120-122. Residual: no WireMock/HTTP-level test through InstagramInsightsClient.businessDiscovery, so a future edit to the fields= string is unpinned.

findings.title: [Q1.2] firstUsableBrandToken does not filter authPath, so a future INSTAGRAM_LOGIN brand row would 503 instead of falling back
findings.issue: Business Discovery and /me/accounts are FACEBOOK_LOGIN-only (InstagramInsightsClient.java:112-113, MetaGraphApiClient.java:92-94), but firstUsableBrandToken selects on revoked+expiry alone. Unreachable today only because no writer sets authPath on a workspace-scoped row; a future brand IG-Login flow silently breaks lookup and Marketplace enrichment with a misleading 503.
findings.fix: Add .filter(t -> t.getAuthPath() == MetaAuthPath.FACEBOOK_LOGIN) to firstUsableBrandToken, mirroring the creator-side filter at ExternalCreatorService.java:293, so an unusable row falls through to the creator fallback.
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/ExternalCreatorService.java:243-248 adds .filter(t -> t.getAuthPath() == MetaAuthPath.FACEBOOK_LOGIN) before the expiry filter, mirroring the creator-side filter at :448. Compiles clean.

findings.title: [Q1.3] Borrowed creator token makes brand lookup traffic throttle that creator's own metrics polling
findings.issue: resolveBusinessDiscoveryCaller picks an arbitrary creator's FACEBOOK_LOGIN token; MetaGraphApiClient keys rate limiting on that creator's igBusinessAccountId (MetaGraphApiClient.java:110), the same key MetricsPollingJob throttles on (MetricsPollingJob.java:204) and marks limited (L253). Brand Discover volume can silently stall an unrelated creator's analytics ingestion, and no Meta platform-terms review of cross-user token reuse exists in wiki/.
findings.fix: Introduce an Influora-owned IG Business system caller (new influora.meta.system-ig-* properties + stored token) as the preferred caller ahead of the creator fallback, and escalate the cross-user-token question to Swapnil for a platform-terms ruling before App Review.
findings.evidence: Code half correct: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/ExternalCreatorService.java:558-561 prefers the system caller, :588-598 resolves it, bound with real placeholders at influora-api/src/main/resources/application.yml:408-409. STILL OPEN because deploy/utho/generate-env.sh:146-147 ships META_SYSTEM_IG_USER_ID and META_SYSTEM_IG_ACCESS_TOKEN blank on every target, so resolveSystemCaller returns null and the borrowed creator token at :569-583 is the production path. Also awaiting a Swapnil ruling on Meta cross-user token reuse (escalated SHARED_CONTEXT.md:342).

findings.title: [Q1.4] Handle rename permanently breaks lookup with an unrecoverable 409; concurrent first-lookup race loses one caller
findings.issue: lookup resolves by ig_username only, then applies bd.id(). If another row already holds that ig_account_id (creator renamed on Instagram) the save violates uk_external_creators_ig_account; two brands looking up the same new handle concurrently violate uk_external_creators_username. Both become a 409 DATA_INTEGRITY_VIOLATION rendered to the brand as 'data conflict', with no retry and no reconciliation - the renamed creator can never be looked up again.
findings.fix: In lookup, resolve by externalCreatorRepository.findByIgAccountId(bd.id()) (ExternalCreatorRepository.java:22) before falling back to findByIgUsernameIgnoreCase, and update ig_username on that row (rename reconciliation). Wrap the save in a catch of DataIntegrityViolationException that re-reads by ig_account_id then ig_username and returns the winning row.
findings.evidence: Race half closed and the pin discriminates. The recovery re-read is now wrapped in runInNewTransaction at influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/ExternalCreatorService.java:469-475, whose TransactionTemplate is built PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW at :155 and executed at :165-167, so a fresh EntityManager/JDBC connection and a fresh REPEATABLE READ snapshot are established AFTER the winner's commit and the winning row is visible; orElseThrow is unreachable for this scenario. Racy save isolated at :449-453, rename forced false at :476 so no stale write follows. No custom PlatformTransactionManager bean exists (JpaTransactionManager default), so REQUIRES_NEW genuinely suspends the outer tx. Javadoc reconciled at :406-414, :460-468, :506-514. PINS: ExternalCreatorServiceTest.java:342 lookup_concurrentRace_returnsWinningRowInsteadOf409, with transaction-boundary assertions at :388 verify(transactionManager, times(2)).getTransaction(any()) and the InOrder chain at :389-393 (getTransaction -> saveAndFlush -> getTransaction -> findByIgAccountId); non-vacuity verified structurally -- reverting to the plain re-read leaves exactly one getTransaction and the pin fails. Outer-tx non-poisoning pinned by real @DataJpaTest ExternalCreatorServiceRaceRollbackIsolationTest.java:213. CHECKS RE-RUN BY PRIYA: mvn -o -DskipTests compile BUILD SUCCESS; mvn -o test-compile BUILD SUCCESS; mvn -o test -Dtest=ExternalCreatorServiceTest,ExternalCreatorServiceRaceRollbackIsolationTest -> 12/12, 0 failures, 0 errors. RESIDUAL (follow-up ticket, shares Q3.4's root, not a Q1.4 reopen): connect()'s recovery re-read at ExternalCreatorService.java:716-719 is still a plain ambient-snapshot read.

findings.title: [Q1.5] Instagram tab ships no q/follower filters (contract TASKS.md:157) and the backend filter would silently hide every un-enriched row

When added, ExternalCreatorSpecs.java:33-39 emits followers >= ? / <= ?, which is UNKNOWN for NULL - every ADMIN_IMPORT stub and every META_MARKETPLACE row (followers always null, ExternalCreatorService.java:192-200) would vanish with no explanation.
findings.fix: Add the search + follower-range controls to InstagramCreatorsTab and pass q/minFollowers/maxFollowers through fetchList; in ExternalCreatorSpecs wrap the follower predicates as cb.or(cb.isNull(followers), cb.ge(...)) or gate them behind an explicit 'only creators with known followers' toggle, and mark unknown-follower cards the way engagement renders '-' rather than 0.
findings.evidence: src/components/brand/discover/creator-discovery.tsx:2113-2129 passes q/minFollowers/maxFollowers into api.externalCreators.list (src/lib/api.ts:1910-1912 -> ExternalCreatorController.java:40-42); NULL followers preserved by cb.or(cb.isNull(...)) at influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/repository/ExternalCreatorSpecs.java:42-46; unknown counts render em dash at creator-discovery.tsx:1941-1943. findings.issue: All three applySync call sites (ExternalCreatorService.java:196-202 Marketplace, :263 Business Discovery, AdminCreatorConnectionService.java:344-352 admin import) pass null for engagementRate, and applySync (ExternalCreator.java:200) only writes on non-null. findings.title: [Q2.2] Half-guarded JOINED card: "Create campaign" checks linkedCreatorProfileId, "View profile" links to /brand/creators/ with an empty id
findings.issue: L1952 ORs status==='JOINED' with the server's verifiedWithInfluora, admitting a JOINED-but-unlinked row the server flag excludes. The Create-campaign button defends against it (L1996-2001) but the View-profile Link at L1993 falls back to an empty id and navigates to a dead route. The state is unreachable through code (ExternalCreator.markJoined, ExternalCreator.java:231-236, always sets both), so this is defensive-code inconsistency, not a live break.
findings.fix: Drop the OR and trust the server flag: `const verified = creator.verifiedWithInfluora;`. If the defensive OR is kept deliberately, render "View profile" only when linkedCreatorProfileId is non-null, matching the Create-campaign guard.
findings.evidence: src/components/brand/discover/creator-discovery.tsx:1976-1981 now reads `const verified = creator.verifiedWithInfluora;` (the server's computed flag), footer branch at :2025-2036; server flag at influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/ExternalCreatorService.java:621 requires JOINED AND linkedCreatorProfileId != null.

findings.title: [Q2.3] 409 CREATOR_ALREADY_ON_INFLUORA carries linkedCreatorProfileId that the FE type system discards — brand hits a dead-end toast
findings.issue: ApiErrorBody.creatorAlreadyOnInfluora (ApiErrorBody.java:62-64) puts linkedCreatorProfileId on the wire and api.ts:1918-1922 tells callers to use it, but ApiErrorPayload (api.ts:215-224) never declares the field and both ApiError throw sites (api.ts:562-567, :631-636) populate `details` only via extractInsufficientFundsDetails (api.ts:253-264), so the id is unreachable. submitConnect (creator-discovery.tsx:2154-2160) therefore shows a generic destructive toast and the card still reads "Connect this creator". TASKS.md L87 specified this payload for a create-campaign CTA that does not exist.
findings.fix: Add `linkedCreatorProfileId?: string` to ApiErrorPayload, widen ApiError.details to a discriminated union (or add a sibling `creatorAlreadyOnInfluora` extractor next to extractInsufficientFundsDetails), and branch in submitConnect on err.code === 'CREATOR_ALREADY_ON_INFLUORA' to patch the card to JOINED and toast with a Create-campaign action. If the CTA is not wanted, delete the field from ApiErrorBody and the api.ts doc comment instead of shipping an unread payload.
findings.evidence: src/lib/api.ts:221-227 adds linkedCreatorProfileId to ApiErrorPayload, :277-285 to ApiError, populated at all three envelope throw sites; consumer branches at src/components/brand/discover/creator-discovery.tsx:2206-2226 and patches the card to JOINED/verified/linked in place. Wire shape at influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/common/GlobalExceptionHandler.java:69-77.

findings.title: [Q2.4] API outage on the Instagram tab renders the honest-empty state: "No Instagram creators sourced yet" instead of an error
findings.issue: fetchList treats only err.status === 503 as unavailable (L2062), but GET /creators/external never returns 503 (ExternalCreatorService.java:100-125 swallows all Marketplace failures at L164-173). A 502 from nginx becomes ApiError('SERVER_UNAVAILABLE', status 502) via parseEnvelope (api.ts:580-595) and a dropped connection is a TypeError; both clear listCreators and set listError, after which showEmpty (L2165-2167) is true and the tab shows data-testid="instagram-empty" / "No Instagram creators sourced yet". listError is rendered only in the non-empty branch (L2274-2276), so it never displays on a first-load failure — the brand is told the data does not exist when the server is down. F-0259/F-0260 empty-state-honesty class.
findings.fix: Add a distinct listFailed state: treat err.code === 'SERVER_UNAVAILABLE', status 502/503/504, and non-ApiError network errors as unavailable/failed, and gate showEmpty on `!listError && !listFailed` so a failed load renders an error panel with Retry, never the empty state. Add a vitest that a 502 and a rejected fetch each render the error state and not instagram-empty.
findings.evidence: src/components/brand/discover/creator-discovery.tsx:2113-2125 routes a 502 ApiError and a TypeError to setListFailed/setListError; :2241-2243 excludes showFailed from showEmpty and renders the failure branch first; error panel + working Retry at :2329-2343. Pins creator-discovery.instagram.test.tsx:188-205 (502) and :207-217 (dropped connection), both asserting instagram-empty is NOT rendered.

findings.title: [Q2.5] Brand connection-request panel renders no dates: handledAt is on the wire and unused, invitedAt is on no brand DTO at all
findings.issue: ConnectionRequestResponse already ships createdAt (ExternalCreatorDtos.java:45) and handledAt (:47), mirrored at api.ts:1858,1860, but the My-connection-requests panel (creator-discovery.tsx:2205-2222) renders only the handle and the status label — a brand cannot tell a 3-week-stale CONTACTED from yesterday's. Separately, external_creators.invited_at (set in ExternalCreator.java:225-227) is absent from both brand DTOs (ExternalCreatorDtos.java:19-36 and :38-49), so "an invite was actually emailed" never reaches the brand, and the amber badge collapsing UNVERIFIED/INVITED (L1904-1920) has no signal to split on.
findings.fix: Render relative createdAt and handledAt on each request row (no backend change needed). Add `Instant invitedAt` to ExternalCreatorResponse, populate it in toResponse (ExternalCreatorService.java:413-435), mirror it in api.ts's ExternalCreator, and give INVITED its own badge copy ("Invited to Influora") with the date.
findings.evidence: src/components/brand/discover/creator-discovery.tsx:2293-2298 renders relative createdAt and handledAt on each request row; INVITED gets its own badge at :1925-1931 fed by creator.invitedAt at :2005; invitedAt appended to ExternalCreatorResponse at influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/ExternalCreatorService.java:642 and mirrored on the TS type in src/lib/api.ts.

findings.title: [Q3.1] Admin connection-request email is dark on every deploy target (ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL blank/unset)
findings.issue: generate-env.sh writes ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL= and both compose files pass ${ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL} with no :- default, so NotificationListener.java:638-644 WARNs and skips. Step 3 of the flow (enquiry reaches the admin team) never fires; the admin console page is the only way a request is ever seen.
findings.fix: Set a real address in the deploy .env (and a :-default in both compose files), then prove one delivery end-to-end; until then treat the admin console as the sole notification channel and say so in the handoff.
findings.evidence: No code change. deploy/utho/generate-env.sh:153 still writes ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL= blank, and both compose files default to empty (deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho.yml:230, deploy/hostinger/docker-compose.hostinger.yml:201), so NotificationListener WARN-and-skips on every deploy target and step 3 of the flow never fires. Escalation at SHARED_CONTEXT.md:343 is accurate but is not a fix. TO CLOSE: ops provisions a real inbox, AND add the startup assertion / deploy gate that fails loudly on blank (precedent: generate-env.sh:154-156 CompanyTaxStartupValidator) or record an explicit Swapnil ruling that WARN-and-skip is accepted. RULING 2026-09-03 (Swapnil, via chat): accept WARN-and-skip. Admin dashboard (GET /admin/creator-connections, AdminCreatorConnectionService.list) is the sole channel for this enquiry; ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL stays unset intentionally. No code change required or wanted. Do not re-flag this as an open defect; SMTP/MSG91 setup remains open for other email flows (OTP, deal notifications) but is decoupled from this decision.

findings.title: [Q3.2] Join notification goes to a stale requester and is silently lost if that user was removed
findings.issue: reopen() keeps the original requestedByUserId, so after a DECLINED reopen by a different member the brand.connected_creator_joined email (ExternalCreatorLinkService.java:128) reaches the wrong colleague; if that user is gone, emailOf returns null, NotificationService.java:128-131 queues nothing, and joined_notified_at is stamped regardless — the headline 'creator joined' promise is dropped with only a WARN.
findings.fix: Take requestedByUserId in reopen(message, userId) and set it from principal; in the listener, fall back to the workspace owner/admins when emailOf(userId) is null, and only stamp joined_notified_at when an email was actually queued.
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/domain/entity/CreatorConnectionRequest.java:139-151 re-stamps requestedByUserId on reopen and no longer clears joinedNotifiedAt; the single production call site is wired at ExternalCreatorService.java:516. Undeliverable case falls back to workspace OWNER then ADMIN at NotificationListener.java:140-159, and markJoinedNotified is now conditional on a resolved recipient. Pins CreatorConnectionRequestTest.java:38-52, NotificationListenerTest.java:106-128 and :130-151. NOTE for the merge owner: ExternalCreatorService.java is outside this package's file list -- re-confirm :516 survives whichever concurrent package owns that file.

findings.title: [Q3.3] Admin connection-request email has no retry: a transient SMTP failure loses the notification permanently
findings.issue: The @Async listener calls Msg91EmailClient directly; sendTemplateEmail returning false (Msg91EmailClient.java:132-148) produces one log.error and nothing else — no outbox row, no retry, no marker on creator_connection_requests. The admin console is the only recovery and nothing tells anyone to look.
findings.fix: Queue an EmailOutbox row with userId=null (the pre-account recipient path the client already supports) so EmailWorker retries with backoff, keeping the in-app half suppressed as today.
findings.evidence: The prescribed EmailOutbox row with a null userId is impossible without a migration (EmailOutbox.java:29 nullable=false, V18__email_outbox.sql:19 FK). Substitute closes both harms: bounded retry at NotificationListener.java:709-720 (0/1s/3s) and a durable error_log row on give-up at :722-745, surfaced on the live /admin/errors route (src/pages/admin-console.tsx:71); sink is safe (ErrorLogService.java:50-83 REQUIRES_NEW + total catch). Pins NotificationListenerTest.java:164/179/193. Residuals to ticket: the email itself is still non-durable, and Thread.sleep pins an @Async pool thread up to 4s per failing event.

findings.title: [Q3.4] Concurrent connect returns 409 DATA_INTEGRITY_VIOLATION instead of the contracted idempotent 200
findings.issue: Double-click/two-tab POSTs race past findByWorkspaceIdAndExternalCreatorId; the loser violates uk_ccr_workspace_creator and falls through to GlobalExceptionHandler.java:110-115 (409 DATA_INTEGRITY_VIOLATION). The brand sees 'Could not send request' and a card still offering 'Connect this creator' although the request was created. Not a 500, and only one admin email (the loser rolls back before the AFTER_COMMIT listener).
findings.fix: Wrap the save in try/catch (DataIntegrityViolationException) as CreatorDiscoveryService.java:493-499 does, re-read the row, and return it as the idempotent 200 the contract specifies; also disable the dialog's Send button on the pending promise.
findings.evidence: connect()'s saveAndFlush runs in the REQUIRES_NEW template at influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/ExternalCreatorService.java:620-623 and the DataIntegrityViolationException is caught and resolved by re-read at :634-641, returning the idempotent 200. FE double-click path removed at src/components/brand/discover/creator-discovery.tsx:2516 (disabled={connectSubmitting}). Pins ExternalCreatorServiceTest.java:360 and ExternalCreatorServiceRaceRollbackIsolationTest.java:166. Residual (follow-up ticket, shares a root with Q1.4): the loser's re-read still runs in the outer transaction's snapshot, so a genuinely simultaneous two-tab pair can still 409.

findings.title: [Q3.5] No per-workspace cap or rate limit on POST /creators/external/{id}/connect
findings.issue: connect accepts any external_creators id regardless of source/status (ExternalCreatorService.java:313-328) and list exposes every row unfiltered (L111); one brand can create a request per creator across the whole table, each publishing an admin email (L361-373). No annotation, filter or counter caps this.
findings.fix: Add a config-driven per-workspace daily cap on new/reopened requests returning 429, plus digest/batching of admin.creator_connection_requested when several fire inside a window.
findings.evidence: enforceDailyConnectCap at influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/ExternalCreatorService.java:566-582, called on reopen (:515) and on new (:519) and deliberately skipped for the idempotent already-exists return (:511-513), so the TASKS.md:87 idempotency contract is preserved. 429 CREATOR_CONNECT_RATE_LIMITED reaches the client via GlobalExceptionHandler.java:42; config at application.yml:287-288. Pin ExternalCreatorServiceTest.java:328-358, verified non-vacuous (builder stamps createdAt at entity line 232). Admin-email digest/batching half not built -- follow-up, not a reopen.

findings.issue: apiRequest returns {success:false} instead of throwing (api-contracts.ts:95-105), so onSuccess fires for 404/409/500 too. It skips invalidation but still calls setActiveAction(null) at :282. There is no onError, no success toast, and no failure banner — an invite that never sent looks identical to one that did.

findings.title: [Q4.2] Invite email hard-codes brand_name to 'A brand' although the workspace name is already resolved
findings.issue: The creator.join_invitation subject templates {{brand_name}} (EmailTemplateRegistry.java:337) but invite() passes the literal 'A brand', so every invite reads 'A brand wants to work with you on Influora'. The request row has workspaceId and toDtos already loads Workspace.getName() at :504 — the data was in hand.
findings.fix: Pass the CreatorConnectionRequest into sendJoinInvitationEmail, look up the Workspace by request.getWorkspaceId(), and use its name; fall back to 'A brand' only when the workspace row is gone.
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/admin/AdminCreatorConnectionService.java:255 threads the CreatorConnectionRequest into sendJoinInvitationEmail, which resolves the real Workspace by request.getWorkspaceId() and uses its name at :266-275; the 'A brand' fallback is correctly narrowed to a missing workspace or a null/blank name. Pins AdminCreatorConnectionServiceTest.java:180-209 (captures the actual Msg91 payload, asserts the real workspace name is present and 'A brand' is absent) and :211-237.

findings.title: [Q4.3] Bulk import runs up to 50 blocking Graph calls inside one transaction and reports rate-limited handles as ordinary imports
findings.issue: @Transactional importHandles holds a pooled DB connection across up to 50 synchronous Business Discovery round-trips. MetaRateLimitException is a MetaApiException subclass (MetaRateLimitException.java:6), so the catch at :354 swallows throttling; once MetaGraphApiClient's pre-flight threshold (:109-113) trips, every remaining handle silently becomes an un-enriched stub and ImportResult still counts it as imported, with no retry surface.
findings.fix: Persist the stubs in a short transaction, then enrich out of band (a job keyed on lastSyncedAt IS NULL). Catch MetaRateLimitException separately, stop the loop, and return the un-enriched handles so the admin knows to retry.
findings.evidence: importHandles no longer carries @Transactional (AdminCreatorConnectionService.java:412; no class-level one at :57), so no pooled connection is held across the Graph round-trips -- verified safe (AdminAuditLogService.record has no MANDATORY propagation; ExternalCreator has zero lazy associations). Rate limiting now reports honestly: catch at :484-497 sets the flag and stops the batch, and the un-enriched stub is bucketed into skipped with a reason at :501-521, rendered by src/admin/pages/CreatorConnectionsPage.tsx:613-614. Type confirmed at MetaGraphApiClient.java:109-112. Pin AdminCreatorConnectionServiceTest.java:154. Residuals to ticket: no out-of-band enrichment job, and a rate-limited re-sync of an EXISTING row is counted in neither imported nor skipped (:519 sits inside if (wasNew)).

findings.title: [Q4.4] Admin import accepts unvalidated handles: garbage is persisted brand-visibly and one long line rolls back the whole batch
findings.issue: normalizeUsername (:553-556) applies neither ExternalCreatorService.USERNAME_PATTERN (ExternalCreatorService.java:58) nor the 80-char column limit (ExternalCreator.java:44). Invalid handles are interpolated raw into the Graph path (InstagramInsightsClient.java:117-122) and, after Meta rejects them, still saved at :359 and counted as imported; an 81-char handle fails at flush, returning 409 and discarding all 50. There is no delete endpoint (AdminExternalCreatorController.java has only GET and POST /import), so a bad stub is permanent and shows in brand Discover.
findings.fix: Promote USERNAME_PATTERN to a shared validator and apply it plus a length<=80 check in the import loop, routing rejects into ImportResult.skipped instead of persisting them; add an audit-logged DELETE /admin/external-creators/{id} guarded when connection requests reference the row.
findings.evidence: IMPORT_USERNAME_PATTERN at AdminCreatorConnectionService.java:76 matches ExternalCreatorService.java:61 byte-for-byte and is applied at :438-446, i.e. before the Graph path interpolation and before the persist, routing rejects into skipped; the 80-char cap matches the ig_username VARCHAR(80) column and importHandles is no longer @Transactional, so one bad row cannot discard the batch. Guarded delete added at :346-385 (SUPER_ADMIN/ADMIN + MFA, CONFLICT when referenced, audit-logged) with the endpoint at influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/web/AdminExternalCreatorController.java:60-66. Pins AdminCreatorConnectionServiceTest.java:108-119, :120-131, :244-256, :257-268.

findings.title: [Q4.5] AdminConnection TS type declares four fields non-null that the Java record emits as null
findings.issue: brandName (:617), requestedByEmail (:619), igUsername (:621) and creatorStatus (:626) are typed `string`, but toDtos emits null for each when the workspace, user or external-creator row is missing (AdminCreatorConnectionService.java:504,506,508,513). Only external_creator_id has an FK (TASKS.md L73). CreatorConnectionsPage.tsx:447 calls c.igUsername.charAt(0) with no guard — the same FE-asserts-a-field-the-record-may-not-send class as F1/PHONE-0829 P3.
findings.fix: Widen all four to `| null` in admin.types.ts and render explicit fallbacks (an em dash for brandName at :442 and :188, a safe initial at :447); separately, page the external-creators table and wire its status/q filters, and replace the in-memory search IN-list (:434-445) with a join.

findings.title: [Q5.2] Meta token refresh re-runs the JOINED hook: joined_at drifts, Discover re-sorts, and a reopened request re-emails the brand
findings.issue: MetaTokenRefreshService.java:190-201 calls the 8-arg storeCreatorToken every ~55 days with igBusinessAccountId set, so ExternalCreatorLinkService.java:106 calls markJoined again on an already-JOINED row. markJoined re-stamps joinedAt and updatedAt unconditionally, so (a) the real join date is lost, and (b) ExternalCreatorService.java:115 sorts updatedAt DESC, so a token refresh bumps that creator to the top of every brand's Discover list. Separately, CreatorConnectionRequest.reopen:119 nulls joinedNotifiedAt, which is the exact field NotificationListener.java:675-681 uses for idempotency — a reopened request will be re-flipped and re-emailed by a background refresh.
findings.fix: Make markJoined idempotent: no-op (or only set linkedCreatorProfileId) when status is already JOINED and linkedCreatorProfileId equals the incoming id, so joinedAt/updatedAt are set once. Preserve joinedAt the way MetaTokenStorage preserves createdAt (F-0173). Do not clear joinedNotifiedAt in reopen(); keep it as a permanent 'this brand has already been told' marker, or gate the hook on a real identity change rather than every token write.
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/domain/entity/ExternalCreator.java:239-250 makes markJoined idempotent (skips the joinedAt/updatedAt re-stamp when already JOINED and linked to the same profile), so a ~55-day Meta token refresh can no longer drift joinedAt or bump the row to the top of Discover's updatedAt DESC sort; no @PreUpdate re-stamps behind the guard. reopen no longer nulls joinedNotifiedAt (CreatorConnectionRequest.java:139-151), so no second brand email. Pins ExternalCreatorTest.java:44-65 and :67-79, CreatorConnectionRequestTest.java:65-83.

findings.title: [Q5.3] JOINED hook discards the IG business account id at the one site that has it from a real Meta sync
findings.issue: syncPlatforms already resolves tokenRow.getIgBusinessAccountId() at PortfolioService.java:276 before calling upsertPlatformStat at :313, but the hook call at :367-369 passes igAccountId=null, so ExternalCreatorLinkService falls back to the case-insensitive ig_username branch (:79-83). That branch cannot match a renamed handle, cannot match a handle containing a dot after normalization, and is the weaker of the two keys. The strongest available identity signal in the whole feature is thrown away.
findings.fix: Thread the resolved igBusinessAccountId from syncPlatforms (PortfolioService.java:276) into upsertPlatformStat and pass it as the third argument at :367-369, so the hook takes the exact ig_account_id branch. Keep metric.getUsername() as the secondary key.
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/portfolio/PortfolioService.java:276 resolves igBusinessAccountId (hard-failing NOT_CONNECTED at :277-282), threads it through upsertPlatformStat at :313-316 / :330-331 and into the hook at :379-390; consumed at ExternalCreatorLinkService.java:94-97, which takes the findByIgAccountId branch and sets matchedByAccountId=true -- so this site both gets the exact-id match and legitimately satisfies the Q5.4 first-link guard. upsertPlatformStat has exactly one caller, so no path reaches the hook with a null id from a real Meta sync.

findings.title: [Q5.4] Identity spoof: claiming an Influora username equal to an external Instagram handle links the impostor to the external creator row and emails the brand to hire them
findings.issue: applyUsername feeds an unverified Influora vanity handle into ExternalCreatorLinkService.onCreatorIdentified, which matches it against external_creators.ig_username (:79-83). Reachable by any authenticated creator via PATCH profile (CreatorProfileService.java:62-68) or portfolio update (PortfolioService.java:204-210) with no Meta connection and no proof of controlling the Instagram account. The relink guard at ExternalCreatorLinkService.java:89-102 only fires when linkedCreatorProfileId is already set, which is never true for an UNVERIFIED/INVITED row. Result: the external row flips to JOINED with the impostor's linked_creator_profile_id, every open connection request flips to JOINED, and the brand receives 'X joined Influora' with campaign_url carrying the impostor's creatorId (NotificationListener.java:683-695) — an impersonation that terminates in a paid collaboration.
findings.fix: Remove the onCreatorIdentified call at CreatorProfileService.java:180 — an Influora username is not an Instagram identity and must never be a match key. Restrict the hook to Meta-verified sources only: MetaTokenStorage.java:346 (id + username from the OAuth exchange) and PortfolioService.java:367-369 (handle from a real Meta sync, with the ig_account_id threaded through per Q5.3). If a username-only link is still wanted, gate it on the caller holding a non-revoked MetaOAuthToken whose igBusinessAccountId resolves to that handle. Additionally harden ExternalCreatorLinkService.java:89-102 to require an ig_account_id match before ever setting linked_creator_profile_id on a row that has none.
findings.evidence: Layer 1: the spoofable call site is gone -- influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/CreatorProfileService.java:176-183 is a comment block, and the only two production callers of onCreatorIdentified are Meta-verified (MetaTokenStorage.java:359, PortfolioService.java:382). Layer 2 (what makes the verdict safe): ExternalCreatorLinkService.java:130-138 refuses to establish a FIRST link on an unlinked row unless the match came from the ig_account_id branch, so re-adding the call site would still not link. Pin ExternalCreatorLinkServiceTest.java:112-131. Residual: CreatorProfileServiceTest never asserts on the mocked link service -- add verify(..., never()) to pin layer 1 too.

findings.title: [Q5.5] Invite signup_url's handle/ref params are never read at registration, and the hook's 'never fail the caller' catch cannot survive a flush-time constraint violation
findings.issue: AdminCreatorConnectionService.java:244-245 emits /creator/register?ref=influora-invite&handle={igUsername}, but creator-register.tsx imports only useNavigate and Link from react-router-dom and never reads searchParams, so the invite context is discarded — the JOINED flip depends entirely on the creator later connecting Meta. Separately, ExternalCreatorLinkService.java:135-143 swallows the exception but a flush failure has already marked the transaction rollback-only, so the @Transactional proxy at :63 throws UnexpectedRollbackException at commit and the Meta OAuth callback 500s regardless. ExternalCreatorLinkServiceTest.java:34 is pure Mockito with no EntityManager, so this is untested.
findings.fix: Issue a signed single-use invite token bound to the external_creators row (never trust a bare ?handle=), read it in creator-register.tsx, pass it to the register call, and consume it server-side to link the row — the claim must be server-verified, not URL-supplied. For the hook, run it in REQUIRES_NEW (or via an AFTER_COMMIT listener on the caller's transaction) so its failure cannot poison the caller's transaction, and add a @DataJpaTest that inserts a conflicting ig_account_id row and asserts the caller's write still commits.
findings.evidence: The primary scenario -- an invited creator registers by email, never connects Meta, is never linked -- is no longer reachable; every hop traced. FE: src/pages/creator-register.tsx:2 imports useSearchParams, :33 reads invite_token, :35 gates the banner on ref===influora-invite AND a token, :107-113 puts inviteToken on the register payload, which src/lib/api.ts:939 -> :566 JSON.stringify's onto the wire. BE: AuthController.java:94-98 -> CreatorRegisterRequest.java:23-30 (7th component + a 6-arg compatibility ctor) -> AuthService.java:364 consumeInviteToken immediately after the CreatorProfile save -> RegistrationService.java:57-108 re-checks the LIVE row (status still INVITED, invitedAt matches at second precision) -> ExternalCreatorLinkService.linkViaVerifiedInvite :207-235 flips the row JOINED, flips every PENDING/CONTACTED request to JOINED and publishes ConnectedCreatorJoinedEvent, so step 5 of the TASKS.md flow fires for the invite path. ISSUER: AdminCreatorConnectionService.java:282-287 appends &invite_token=issue(id, invitedAt) after markInvited re-stamps invitedAt at :230, so re-invite invalidation is real. SECURITY: InviteTokenService.java:85-93 sets failClosed when the secret is the committed dev default or <32 chars outside dev/test (no active profile also fails closed), logging one ERROR at construction; verify() returns Optional.empty() at :133-143 before any signature work, so nothing can link under the committed literal in prod. DEPLOY: deploy/utho/generate-env.sh:67 emits CREATOR_INVITE_TOKEN_SECRET=$(secret) (openssl rand -base64 48, 48 chars) in the same generated block as JWT_ACCESS_SECRET; passed through at deploy/hostinger/docker-compose.hostinger.yml:190 and deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho.yml:211 -- an unset var resolves to '' (len 0 < 32) and fails closed. FALSIFICATION ATTEMPTS THAT FAILED TO BREAK IT: stray ?handle= with no ref (banner gated on the signed token, so no Q5.4 spoof reintroduced); ordinary registration (undefined key dropped by JSON.stringify, null/blank is a no-op returning false); forged token under the dev default (rejected -- the guard's ERROR line was observed in the mvn run, so the pin is not vacuous). PINS: InviteTokenServiceTest.java:88, :101, :111, :124; RegistrationServiceTest.java:82, :100, :114; creator-register.test.tsx:168, :187, :201. CHECKS RE-RUN BY PRIYA: npx vitest run src/pages/creator-register.test.tsx 6/6; npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit EXIT=0; mvn -o -q test -Dtest=InviteTokenServiceTest,RegistrationServiceTest exit 0. THREE RESIDUALS (follow-up tickets, none reopens the scenario): (a) CreatorRegisterPayload at src/lib/api.ts:818-825 still lacks inviteToken?: string and creator-register.tsx:107 routes around the excess-property check via an untyped local -- brittle if anyone annotates that const or enables exactOptionalPropertyTypes; (b) linkViaVerifiedInvite is REQUIRES_NEW inside the @Transactional creatorRegister (AuthService.java:308), so the JOINED flip and the brand email commit BEFORE registration does, and findById at ExternalCreatorLinkService.java:219 cannot see the uncommitted profile so the email can render a null creator name -- an AFTER_COMMIT listener is the correct shape; (c) stale javadoc at RegistrationServiceTest.java:35 still claims creatorRegister does not call consumeInviteToken yet.

findings.title: [Q6.2] Draft save invites the creator, exposing an unpublished campaign and making the draft undeletable
findings.issue: The post-create invite is gated on `!isEditing && creatorIdParam`, not on the submitted status, so `handleSubmit('DRAFT')` (L481, bound at L1499-1503) creates an INVITED Collaboration on a DRAFT campaign — contradicting both banners ('invited when you publish', campaign-form.tsx:665-666, brand-new-campaign.tsx:112-113). DealService.list (DealService.java:1383) applies no campaign-status filter, so the creator sees the unpublished draft as a deal with a system message. Deleting the draft then 409s on fk_collab_campaign (V6__creators_collaborations.sql:71, GlobalExceptionHandler.java:110-115) with an opaque message.
findings.fix: Gate the invite on `status === 'ACTIVE'` at campaign-form.tsx:524, and stash `creatorIdParam` so a later publish still invites; independently, add a campaign-status guard in CreatorDiscoveryService.invite (L452-505) rejecting DRAFT with a typed error, and exclude DRAFT campaigns from the creator-side deal list.
findings.evidence: Closed at all three layers. FE: src/components/brand/campaigns/campaign-form.tsx:648-661 gates the post-create invite on the submitted status and stashes a DRAFT handoff keyed by the new campaign id, consumed exactly once on a later publish (helpers :82-107). Server guard: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/CreatorDiscoveryService.java:473-478 refuses a DRAFT campaign with a typed CAMPAIGN_NOT_PUBLISHED 409 before any Collaboration row exists. Creator-side backstop: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/DealService.java:157-160 and :1443-1459 drop DRAFT-campaign collaborations for the creator role only. Pins campaign-form-f0290-draft-invite-guard.test.tsx (wizard-driven), CreatorDiscoveryServiceInviteDraftGuardTest, DealServiceCreatorDraftExclusionTest. Residual to file separately: publishing a DRAFT via the detail page's Resume Campaign (brand-campaign-detail.tsx:1104-1106 -> :885) never calls takePendingCreatorInvite, orphaning the stash.

findings.title: [Q6.4] Picking HYPE drops ?creatorId= after the banner promised the invite
findings.issue: choose() navigates to '/brand/campaigns/new/hype' without forwarding the query string, and brand-new-hype-campaign.tsx has no useSearchParams/creatorId handling and no post-create invite (create at L219, navigate away at L221). The handoff banner shown one screen earlier (brand-new-campaign.tsx:222-225) has already told the brand the creator 'will be invited when you publish', so the promise is silently broken for the whole HYPE path.
findings.fix: Forward the param — navigate(`/brand/campaigns/new/hype${creatorId ? `?creatorId=${creatorId}` : ''}`) — and mirror campaign-form.tsx:524-543's post-create invite in brand-new-hype-campaign.tsx after L219; if HYPE is intentionally not invite-capable, suppress the banner for that card and say so on the type tile.
findings.evidence: src/pages/brand-new-campaign.tsx:205-209 builds a query string and forwards creatorId and ig to the HYPE page instead of navigating bare; the type-picker banner at :128-133 no longer makes an unconditional invite promise and carries an explicit Hype caveat; the destination reads the params and renders its own honest banner naming the same @igUsername (src/pages/brand-new-hype-campaign.tsx:72-75, :298-310). Pins brand-new-campaign.hype-handoff.test.tsx:65 (exact forwarded URL) and brand-new-hype-campaign.handoff-banner.test.tsx:65-66 -- both pages had zero coverage before.

findings.title: [Q6.5] Handoff banner shows the Influora username while every upstream surface says @igUsername
findings.issue: The banner resolves the handle via api.creators.getProfile().username (also brand-new-campaign.tsx:100), i.e. the Influora username, while the Discover card and both connect/joined emails identify the creator by @igUsername. The two differ whenever the creator's Influora username differs from their IG handle, and differ necessarily when the IG handle contains a dot (UsernameUtils.VALID allows only [a-z0-9_]), so a brand arriving from the '@foodie.mumbai joined' email reads a banner naming a different account.
findings.fix: Append the external context to the handoff URL at creator-discovery.tsx:1997 (`&ig=<igUsername>&crq=<connectionRequestId>`) and in the joined-email link, and have the banner prefer the `ig` param over profile.username; add the click test described above covering both the banner copy and the post-create invite.
findings.evidence: The named failure scenario -- a brand clicking through from the '@foodie.mumbai joined' email onto a banner naming a different account -- is closed at the source. Both cited call sites now derive from ONE local, so they cannot drift: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/notification/NotificationListener.java:782-786 builds igQueryParam (URLEncoder-encoded, omitted when igUsername is null) and campaignPath, consumed at :792 as campaign_url and at :801 as the in-app deep-link arg of NotificationService.notify (-> createInAppNotification link). A repo-wide grep for 'campaigns/new' across influora-api/src/main returns exactly one hit (:786), so no unpatched second builder survives. The email CTA genuinely consumes it: EmailTemplateRegistry.java:345-352 registers brand.connected_creator_joined with ctaUrlVar 'campaign_url', read at :437 and rendered into the href at :570 (escapeHtml turning & into & is correct attribute encoding; the plain-text branch at :442 uses the raw URL). Consumer half survived concurrent-session churn: src/components/brand/campaigns/campaign-form.tsx:351 reads ig, :357 skips the getProfile resolve when present, :372 prefers it over profile.username, :783 renders it -- so a dotted handle round-trips. Null guard cannot regress anything: ig_username is NOT NULL in both the entity (ExternalCreator.java:44) and the migration (:24) and the sole publisher passes external.getIgUsername(), so the Map.of -> HashMap swap is defensive only. No contract break: TASKS.md:135 specifies the creatorId link and &ig= is purely additive. PINS: NotificationListenerTest.java:168 connectedCreatorJoined_linksCarryEncodedIgHandle asserts BOTH surfaces via ArgumentCaptor using the finding's own dotted handle; :203 connectedCreatorJoined_nullIgUsername_omitsIgParam asserts no &ig=. Both fail against the pre-fix string. CHECKS RE-RUN BY PRIYA: mvn -o -q compile test-compile exit 0; mvn -o test -Dtest=NotificationListenerTest -> Tests run: 8, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, BUILD SUCCESS. RESIDUALS (non-verdict-changing): the test computes its expected param with the same URLEncoder call as production, so it pins presence-of-handle rather than the encoding scheme (harmless -- IG handles are [a-z0-9._], passed through verbatim); and the title/body at NotificationListener.java:796-800 still concatenate '@' + igUsername unguarded, which would read '@null' if the NOT NULL invariant were ever relaxed.

findings.title: [Q7.2] Marketplace upsert discards the IG account id, leaving META_MARKETPLACE rows matchable only by username
findings.issue: upsertFromMarketplace calls applySync only and never applyIgAccountId(creator.id()), although the DTO carries id (CreatorMarketplaceCreatorsResponse.java:20) and the other two upsert paths do call it (ExternalCreatorService.java:262, ExternalCreatorLinkService.java:104). Every Marketplace-sourced row therefore has ig_account_id NULL and can only ever be joined by the weak case-insensitive username match, which a handle rename breaks and an impostor can claim. is_account_verified and insights are parsed and dropped with no destination.
findings.fix: Call external.applyIgAccountId(creator.id()) in upsertFromMarketplace before save (guarding the existing uk_external_creators_ig_account collision the same way the Business Discovery path must), and either persist is_account_verified or drop it and insights from the FIELDS list so the request stops asking for data nothing stores.
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/ExternalCreatorService.java:259-297 resolves by ig_account_id first (:265-266) and calls applyIgAccountId(creator.id()) before save (:279), so META_MARKETPLACE rows are no longer persisted with a permanently-null ig_account_id; the per-creator DataIntegrityViolationException catch at :288-296 is safe here because list() is no longer @Transactional (:132-148), so each saveAndFlush rolls back in its own short transaction. The fetch-and-discard of is_account_verified/insights is gone from CreatorMarketplaceClient.java:27-29; entity guard at ExternalCreator.java:206-211. Minor residual: a row resolved by username whose ig_account_id already differs would be overwritten -- rare given account-id-first resolution.

findings.title: [Q7.3] Marketplace enrichment holds a DB connection across two synchronous Graph calls inside @Transactional list
findings.issue: list() is @Transactional; firstUsableBrandToken (L130) acquires the Hikari connection, then resolvePageAccessToken (L145) and creatorMarketplaceClient.search (L153) each make a Meta round-trip while it is held, on every page of the brand Discover tab. A slow Meta response exhausts the shared pool and degrades the entire API, not just this endpoint. Unreachable today only because the flag defaults false.
findings.fix: Precondition on flipping META_CREATOR_MARKETPLACE_ENABLED: cache the resolved Page access token per workspace (it does not rotate independently of the user token) and move upsertFromMarketplace out of the request transaction into an async job, so list() only ever reads external_creators.
findings.evidence: @Transactional removed from list() (influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/ExternalCreatorService.java:132-148), so no connection is held across the synchronous Graph round-trips; each repository call runs in SimpleJpaRepository's own short transaction. Falsified both wrong-fix modes: ExternalCreator and CreatorConnectionRequest declare zero lazy associations (no @ManyToOne/@OneToMany/FetchType), and spring.jpa.open-in-view is false (application.yml:45) with no @Transactional on ExternalCreatorController -- so no LazyInitializationException and no EntityManager bound outside a transaction. A 10-minute per-workspace page-token cache (:86-90, :222-234) cuts the common case to at most one Graph call. Follow-up (not this failure mode): move upsertFromMarketplace to a real async job.

findings.title: [Q7.4] Empty META_CREATOR_MARKETPLACE_ENABLED from compose fails ConfigurationProperties binding — API will not boot on the live Hostinger VPS
findings.issue: Compose map-form ${META_CREATOR_MARKETPLACE_ENABLED} with no :- default always SETS the container var, empty when the .env lacks it. Spring treats set-but-empty as set, so ${META_CREATOR_MARKETPLACE_ENABLED:false} at application.yml:391 resolves to "" and never uses the default; binding "" to the primitive boolean at MetaApiProperties.java:60 throws BindException -> ConversionFailedException -> 'A null value cannot be assigned to a primitive type'. Verified on spring-boot 3.3.5 / spring-core 6.1.14 (influora-api/pom.xml:10) under JDK 21. The whole API fails to start on the next redeploy of the live Hostinger VPS, whose .env predates this task. Same bare form at deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho.yml:225.
findings.fix: Use META_CREATOR_MARKETPLACE_ENABLED: ${META_CREATOR_MARKETPLACE_ENABLED:-false} and ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL: ${ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL:-} in BOTH compose files, matching CREATOR_COPILOT_ENABLED at hostinger:154 / utho:175. Belt-and-braces: make CreatorMarketplace.enabled a Boolean with a null/blank-coalescing setter, the pattern MetaApiProperties already uses at L157, L174, L182 and L190 — that convention would have absorbed this on its own.
findings.evidence: Closed at two layers. Compose no longer uses the bare map form: deploy/hostinger/docker-compose.hostinger.yml:200 and deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho.yml:229 read ${META_CREATOR_MARKETPLACE_ENABLED:-false} (and ADMIN_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL:- at :201/:230); Compose's :- substitutes when the host var is unset OR empty, so the container var can no longer arrive set-but-empty. Binder belt-and-braces at influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/config/MetaApiProperties.java:76 (nullable Boolean) and :92 (null-coalescing setter), so even a raw empty string binds to false instead of throwing on a primitive. Pin MetaApiPropertiesCreatorMarketplaceBindingTest.java:65 binds the REAL application.yml (:403) through a StandardEnvironment with the var set to "" -- executed green. Two non-blocking notes: no gate asserts the :- defaults survive future compose edits (owed by the .proof-os/gates/ owner), and the test's javadoc misstates :- as substituting only when unset.

findings.title: [Q7.5] findByIgUsernameIgnoreCase forces LOWER() on ig_username, defeating uk_external_creators_username
findings.issue: Spring Data derives lower(e.igUsername) = lower(?1) from the IgnoreCase keyword; a function on the column makes the unique index at migration V20260902120000 L42 unusable, so every lookup full-scans external_creators. The column is already utf8mb4_unicode_ci (migration L45), i.e. case-insensitive by collation, so IgnoreCase adds nothing. Hit on the Marketplace upsert path (ExternalCreatorService.java:188) and the join hook.
findings.fix: Rename to findByIgUsername (usernames are already normalised lower-case, no leading @, per migration L24 and normalizeUsername) so the equality predicate hits uk_external_creators_username directly; the ci collation preserves the case-insensitive semantics.
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/repository/ExternalCreatorRepository.java:44-45 replaces the derived query with an explicit @Query("SELECT e FROM ExternalCreator e WHERE e.igUsername = :igUsername"), which suppresses method-name derivation so no LOWER() is emitted and uk_external_creators_username can be seeked. Falsified both wrong-fix modes: the table is utf8mb4_unicode_ci so plain = is already case-insensitive (V20260902120000__external_creators_connection_requests.sql:45, index at :42), AND both surviving callers normalize before calling (ExternalCreatorLinkService.java:100-101, AdminCreatorConnectionService.java:439) as does every writer -- so the match holds even on a case-sensitive collation, and the untouched callers are a scope choice not a hidden break. Residual: the method keeps an ...IgnoreCase name whose body is not ignore-case (documented with a TODO at :25-42), and no test asserts the emitted SQL lacks LOWER().
